This article compares the 30-day mortality rates following acute surgery for patients with a Charlson Comorbidity Index score of 0 (indicating no severe comorbidities) across Danish regions and hospitals. As a supplementary quality indicator, it isolates surgical and perioperative outcomes by removing the confounding factor of underlying patient comorbidities [^src1].

### Leaders and Trailers
In the current reporting year, the highest observed mortality rates were recorded at [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] (30.0%), [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]] (14.3%), and [[holbaek-sygehus|Holbæk Sygehus]] (13.3%) [^src1]. At the other end of the spectrum, the lowest rates (0.0%) were reported by [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]], [[aalborg-universitetshospital-thisted|Aalborg Universitetshospital, Thisted]], and [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]] [^src1]. The national average for [[danmark|Danmark]] stood at 6.6% [^src1]. 

### Targets and Standards
The data includes a "Standard" column representing the expected mortality rate alongside a 95% confidence interval. Nationally, the expected standard is 6.2% (5.0-7.6), meaning the actual rate of 6.6% falls just outside the upper bound of the expected interval [^src1]. Several hospitals significantly outperformed their standards; for example, [[herlev-og-gentofte-hospital|Herlev og Gentofte Hospital]] achieved an actual mortality of 3.5% against a standard of 11.8% (7.0-18.2), and [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]] recorded 6.1% against a standard of 8.6% (6.1-11.6) [^src1]. Conversely, [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]] reported an actual rate of 14.3%, which sits within its wide standard interval of 14.3% (6.7-25.4) but remains notably high in absolute terms [^src1].

### Trends and Historical Context
While the provided evidence consists of a single dated table section, the table itself includes historical columns for 2022/23 and 2021/22, allowing for internal year-over-year comparisons. Nationally, mortality improved, dropping from 7.8% in 2022/23 to 6.6% in the current year [^src1]. Regional fluctuations are evident: [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] saw a notable decrease from 12.5% to 8.1%, whereas [[sjaelland-region-i-alt|Sjælland Region i alt]] experienced an increase from 7.1% to 8.0% [^src1]. Because this analysis relies on a single dated table section, broader multi-report trend claims across different publication years cannot be established.

### Outliers
[[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] stands out as a major outlier with a current year mortality of 30.0%, despite a standard of 9.1% (0.2-41.3), and a previous year rate of 36.4% [^src1]. This is substantially higher than the national average and other major university hospitals like [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] (3.4% actual) and [[ouh-odense-universitetshospital-odense|OUH Odense Universitetshospital (Odense)]] (10.4% actual) [^src1]. Additionally, small population sizes at hospitals like [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] (10 patients) and [[aalborg-universitetshospital-thisted|Aalborg Universitetshospital, Thisted]] result in wide confidence intervals or missing data, making their 0.0% rates statistically volatile and sensitive to single-case variations [^src1].
